approved_translation: Greed destroys the very source of one's good fortune.
context_summary: Now in a certain place there lived a Brahman named Haridatta. He was a farmer, but poor was the return his labour brought him. And how can you forget the pain and grief at the loss of your son?" So speaking, it gave the Brahman a costly pearl and disappeared. But before it went away it said: "Come back no more." The Brahman took the pearl, and went back home, cursing the folly of his son.
interpretation_boundaries: Keep animal characters naturalistic, not anthropomorphic
Focus on the moral lesson, avoid cultural stereotyping
Do not depict religious figures or deities literally
